baseline_runs.answer:
- Inflation means prices go up over time, so your money buys a little less than it used to.
- It often happens when lots of people want to buy things, or when making things costs more, like gas or wages.
- Stores raise prices to keep up, so your allowance might buy fewer candy bars than last year.

- Inflation means prices go up over time, so the same money buys less stuff.
- It can happen when lots of people want to buy things, or when making things costs more, like fuel or workers' pay.
- Stores raise prices to cover those costs, and then your money doesn't stretch as far at the store.

- Inflation means money buys a little less over time, so prices slowly go up.
- It often happens when lots of people want to buy things, or when making things costs more, like wages or materials.
- Stores raise prices to keep up, so the same toy or snack can cost more than it did before.

- Costs for businesses, like wages, rent, and materials, also rise, and companies usually pass those costs on to shoppers.
